Subject: Onsite tenant pods: routing / holdback question

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're drafting the internal change package for our on-prem tenancy and need a concrete answer on two items before we sign off:

1) Can Redwood's control-plane endpoints be split onto a management-only VLAN that never touches the tenant egress path? Our security team wants absolute separation (no hairpin NAT) between tenant data egress and control telemetry.

2) For the cutover, we prefer a staged holdback: 10% canary, then 50%, then full. We need the recommended guardrails (timeouts, fallback to hosted, metrics to watch) that Redwood recommends for an on-prem canary.

Attaching our requirements doc — acme-tenant-requirements.pdf — that lists compliance constraints and a proposed timeline. Can you confirm whether the architecture you proposed yesterday satisfies the 'no hairpin' requirement and outline the cutover guardrails we should include in the change?

Appreciate it —
Luke
Site Reliability Lead, AcmeCloud
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Onsite Tenant Pods: Control/Data Routing & Cutover Holdback Plan

Luke —

Thanks, and good questions. Short answers up front:
- Yes, we can place Redwood control-plane endpoints on a dedicated management VLAN with a one-way telemetry export (push) to your telemetry ingestion; that keeps tenant egress paths isolated and avoids hairpin NAT.
- We recommend the 10/50/100 canary cadence you describe plus explicit SLO-based rollback triggers (see below).

I've attached a very small sketch (soojin-control-data-sketch.png) and an excerpt of the runbook that shows the guardrails (runbook-excerpt.md). Highlights:
- Control/data demarcation: control-plane (management APIs + KV cache fetches) uses mgmt VLAN, NAT egress only from management-hosted sidecars; data-plane (inference traffic) uses tenant VLANs and egress is blocked from management subnets.
- Observability hooks: require per-tenant token-level tracing, 95th latency, token error-rate, and unexpected-auth failures. Canary thresholds: 95th latency increase > 20% OR error-rate > 0.5% => auto-rollback to previous model/pinned instance.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to hosted Redwood API (multi-tenant hosted tier) is available but must be explicitly enabled by ops during the canary. We add a 'grace period' of 2 minutes after each traffic step to allow systems to settle.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood-run proofing lab: we spin up a representative tenant pod (1 GPU) in your colo and run the canary traffic pattern for 6 hours.
2) Jordan/Neha to provide the control-plane ACL template and egress ACL snippets we used for previous customers.
3) Agree final cutover timeline and rollback contacts.

I'll queue the lab resources once Jordan confirms availability.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Looping in a couple of operational notes (from the network side):

- For 'no hairpin' we recommend: control-plane endpoints on a /26 mgmt subnet with stateless ACLs that only allow outbound TCP 443 to our control egress NAT IPs. No routes from tenant VLANs to that subnet.
- Telemetry: use outbound-only syslog/OTLP to your ingestion IPs; we don't require tenants to host an inbound port.
- DNS: avoid split-horizon for control-plane fqdn — use private DNS entries resolvable only from mgmt VLAN so tenant-facing hosts don't resolve control-plane addresses.

Attached a small CSV with the initial control-plane ACL template; Neha, can you paste this into the runbook and confirm the CIDR ranges?

-J

Thanks — that all looks reasonable and addresses the security team's principal concerns. A couple of quick clarifications before we lock the weekend change window:

- Can you call out the specific metric collection endpoints we should whitelist for OTLP so the SOC team can sign off?
- For the 2-minute grace period, does Redwood maintain a kill-switch to immediately revert routing if we detect a tenant data leak? We need a documented manual rollback in addition to the automated triggers.

I'm attaching our proposed cutover timeline — acme-cutover-timeline.xlsx — which proposes a Friday night 10% canary window with a 24-hour monitoring period before the 50% step. If Redwood can staff an on-call runbook lead for the 10% and 50% steps, we can proceed.

If we can get the OTLP endpoints and the manual rollback play called out, we'll set the RFC.

—Luke
